notes: All 30 source and 33 target ids are partitioned exactly once.

'neither ... nor' is divided by rule 14: the written first לֹא is itself what the opening correlative says and takes 'neither', while the second clause's waw plus its own לֹא fuse as 'nor' under rule 35, headed on the negative. Fusing the pair accounts for both morphemes rather than leaving one unrepresented.
אֵיתָן takes the whole 'with running water' and heads on 'running', which carries the lexeme; heading on the supplied generic 'water' is the competing reading rejected under rule 31.
'the heifer's neck' places the written 'the' on the article of the possessor under rule 29, and עָרַף heads on the complement 'neck' under rule 44, matching DEU.21.6's reading of the same verb.
